name: 1969 NI Parliament
provider: Interim Boundary Commission for Northern Ireland
description: The 52 territorial constituencies of the Parliament of Northern Ireland used at the 1969 general election. Forty-two seats are unchanged from 1929 and keep the 1929 lines. Ten seats in Co. Antrim and Co. Down were redrawn, four of them new (Bangor, Lagan Valley, Larkfield and Newtownabbey), by section 2 and Schedule 1 of the Electoral Law Act (Northern Ireland) 1968, which enacted the Interim Boundary Commission for Northern Ireland's 1967 proposals. The redrawn seats are built from whole 1930 district electoral divisions where possible; four divisions split by the proposal (Ballygomartin, Ballyduff, Monkstown and Crawfordsburn) were cut along the Commission's map line, accurate to about 150 m. The Bangor seat follows the borough as extended on 1 April 1967, plus Groomsport. Checked against Schedule 1 of the Act: the list of seats and their names agree (the Act spells Bannside 'Bann Side'), and the composition of Bann Side, South Antrim, Bangor, Lagan Valley, Mid Down and North Down matches the Act. Antrim, Carrick, Larkfield and Newtownabbey are defined in the Act by divisions of Lisburn Rural District created in 1963 (Suffolk, Andersonstown, Ardmore, Ballygammon, Finaghy, Ladybrook, Upper Malone) and by wards of Newtownabbey Urban District, for which no maps are held, so their lines through the former Belfast Rural District follow the Commission's map and are not confirmed. The Commission's population and electorate figures for the redrawn seats are included. The Queen's University seats, abolished by the same Act, had no territory and are not shown.

references.label: Interim Boundary Commission for Northern Ireland, Report (1967): map showing proposed constituencies and summary of proposals
references.note: Source of the redrawn seats and of the population and electorate figures. The Commission was appointed by warrant of 31 January 1967; its map showing existing constituencies was used as a check against the 1929 layer.

references.label: Electoral Law Act (Northern Ireland) 1968 (1968 c. 20), section 2 and Schedule 1
references.note: Royal Assent 28 Nov 1968. Abolished the Queen's University seats, created Larkfield, Newtownabbey, Bangor and Lagan Valley, and redefined Antrim, Bann Side, Carrick, South Antrim, Mid Down and North Down, for the first general election after its passing. Schedule 1 is repealed and not printed on legislation.gov.uk; the enacted text is reproduced by CAIN (https://cain.ulster.ac.uk/hmso/ela1968.htm). Compared with this map on 31 Oct 2026.

references.label: Bangor Borough (Extension) Order (Northern Ireland) 1966
references.note: Bangor borough as extended from 1 April 1967, used for the Bangor/North Down line. Confirmed by the Ministry of Development Provisional Order Confirmation (Bangor Borough Extension) Act (Northern Ireland) 1966, Royal Assent 6 Dec 1966 (Belfast Gazette issue 2394, 9 Dec 1966, page 465).
